correctness.rationale: Exact normalized beta-prime eigenvalues follow by polar integration. Triadic cylinder counting proves vague convergence and uniform x^delta bounds. Gamma-ratio asymptotics plus the exponential near-zero and polynomial far-tail controls yield the locally uniform inverse-gamma scaling limit. Multiplicative Cantor scaling gives period three; the Fourier transform Gamma(s+i omega) has no zeros, so the singular log-Cantor measure forces a nonconstant profile. The uniform positive power law gives compactness, operator-norm convergence and the exact Schatten threshold; numeric finite comparisons independently check normalization but are not treated as proof.

value.rationale: At critical Cantor scaling the original finite-stage norm estimate is only order-one. The new object is a well-defined compact operator with boundary-accumulating infinite hyperbolic area, and the exact high-mode spectral asymptotic has a provably nonconstant log-periodic leading coefficient. The ensuing sharp Schatten and weak-endpoint transition precisely quantifies residual compactness; both coefficient structure and spectral ideal threshold are natural, reusable data not captured by finite-stage norm bounds.
